paper_title: Direct Detection of Dark Photon Dark Matter with the James Webb Space Telescope
coupling_convention: epsilon x (rho_A'/rho_DM)^0.5, i.e. kinetic mixing chi normalized to full local DM density, dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis
notes: Paper proposes DPDM detection via a modified JWST mirror configuration during ground testing of future space telescopes. This is a PROJECTED sensitivity (red dashed curves in Fig. 4), not an observed limit, since JWST is already in space and its current configuration cannot detect DPDM-induced photons. Quoted sensitivity: epsilon ~ 1e-12 to 1e-14 over 10-500 THz (mass ~0.041-2.07 eV, converted via m[eV]=4.136e-15*f[Hz]) at 95% C.L. Exact numerical values are only shown in Fig. 4 (not tabulated); intermediate data points here are approximate interpolations between the endpoints stated in the abstract/text and should be treated as indicative of the envelope only. MIRI covers the low-frequency (10-60 THz) portion and NIRSpec the high-frequency (100-500 THz) portion. Local DM density value not explicitly stated in the provided text, so dm_density_assumed left null despite this being a DM haloscope-type search. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 shows 95% C.L. projected sensitivity (red dashed) for the modified JWST configuration: left section JWST-MIRI (~0.045-0.23 eV, floor ~2.5-3.5e-13), right section JWST-NIR (~0.24-2.07 eV, floor ~2e-14 rising to ~1e-13 with spiky features near 0.9-1.2 eV).
